instruction: Write a product description in the Spices, Inc. brand voice for the following spice.
input:
Name: Organic California Garlic Powder
Category: Staple Spices
Characteristics: Classic Chili Spices, Organic, Umami, White Label Products
output:
Organic California Garlic Powder, Allium sativum, is also called organic garlic powder grown in USA, California garlic powder, or USA garlic powder. Garlic powder is the product of fresh garlic that is dehydrated and then milled to the desired fineness. It has an essential oil content of .1% - .25%.

Garlic is a bulbous perennial plant most likely native to Central Asia, in the region that included Turkmenistan and Tajikistan. It was already in everyday use 5,000 years ago; by the 3rd millennium BC it had spread across the Mediterranean, making its way into Egyptian kitchens and preserved in the pyramids.

Today, Americans alone consume over 250 million pounds of garlic annually. It is a member of the genus Allium and is close cousins with leeks, chives, shallots, and onions. You can browse our main garlic page to see the varieties of garlic we have available.

1 fresh garlic clove = 1/8 teaspoon of garlic powder or ¼ teaspoon of granulated garlic or ½ teaspoon of minced garlic.

Unlike fresh garlic, which tends to have a very upfront flavor, Garlic Powder adds more subtle complexity and umami to anything it is added to. It can be used in many ways; we regularly supply butchers, creameries, and olive oil shops with Organic California Garlic Powder.

Flavor Profile

Organic California Garlic Powder has garlic’s pronounced mustard-like pungency without the sharp, almost spicy edge that fresh garlic can deliver. The dehydrating and milling process mellows the flavor and leaves the powder with a touch of sweetness.

How to Use

Garlic powder works in any recipe that calls for dried or fresh garlic. This fine powder is great to use as a finisher—sprinkle on your pizza, add an extra flourish to sunny-side eggs, or with salt and pepper to top your perfectly grilled steak. It blends seamlessly with ground meats, so use this to add some garlicky warmth to a Tex-Mex Lasagna or meatballs. It’s also excellent whisked into a pungent marinade for Cajun Chicken Wings. It’s a perfect seasoning base for Chicken Sofrito Stew and shows off its Asian side when mixed into Simple Sesame Chicken.

Because it is a pure garlic flavor, it should be used with a light hand at first.

Garlic powder is a popular ingredient in spice blends. It is used to season beef, chicken, chutneys, curried dishes, ketchup, mayonnaise, pickles, popcorn, pork, roasted nuts, salad dressings, sauces, seafood, spaghetti, stews, and vegetables.

Garlic Powder pairs well with basil, beans, ginger, greens, onions, spinach, and turmeric.

Category: Staple Spices

output:
Organic California Granulated Onion, Allium cepa, is also referred to as organic granulated onion, bulk organic onion granules, or organic onion granulates. It is a member of the Allium family, and is a close relative of garlic, leeks, shallots, and bulbed flowers like the lily.
Our organic granulated onions are grown and processed in California. When they reach peak ripeness they are picked, dehydrated, and ground into easy to pour, easy to blend granules that deliver the concentrated flavor of sweet onions.
Bulk organic granulated onion is popular with seasoning companies, food manufacturers, particularly those who specialize in salsa, sauces, and jerky. It is also popular with restaurants, like taco food trucks and classic American places.
1 Tablespoon Granulated Onion = 1 medium onion, chopped.
We have a wide range of onion products available in both conventional and organic offerings. Please see our onion feature page for more information.

Flavor Profile
Sweet and pungent, with a pleasantly acrid edge.

How To Use
We recommend using Organic California Granulated Onion when you want to get the taste of onion without chunky texture. It will mix seamlessly into a roux or savory bechamel, so use it to season Chicken and Sausage Gumbo or your favorite mac & cheese. This is great to whisk into the vinaigrette for a Grilled Portobello and Radicchio Salad. Enhance the savory flavor of Garlic and Herb Mushrooms by sprinkling over the mushrooms. This spice brings aromatic complexity to vegetable dishes, like Roasted Sweet Potatoes. Add even more depth to Herbed Chicken that’s spiked with garlic and herbs. Organic California Granulated Onion blends easily into the stuffing for Black Bean Stuffed Peppers. It can also round out the seasonings in a DIY Dry Rib Rub. Use Organic California Granulated Onion anywhere you want the smooth, blendable flavor of sweet onion.

Organic California Paprika is a very mild chile powder, with a maximum Scoville Heat Unit (SHU) measurement of 500 and a premium ASTA value of 120. It is made from various cultivars of Capsicum annuum chiles that meet the correct heat and color requirements. Also known as organic paprika, paprika organic, bulk paprika, or organic paprika powder, paprika chiles are relished for their vibrant color and mildly pungent, peppery yet sweet flavor. Organic California Paprika is also known as organic paprika, paprika organic, bulk paprika, or organic paprika powder.
Paprika varieties are distinguished by their high levels of red pigments called capsanthin and capsorubin that are in the walls or pericarp of the fruit. Sweet paprika is made primarily of pericarp; the innards, seeds, and stems are discarded.

food trucks;
taco, Middle Eastern, and pizza restaurants;
independent spice shops; and
seasoning companies

Organic California Paprika has very little heat and is earthy and sweet with a fresh, almost green flavor.

Category: Spices

output:
Organic Cardamom Seeds, Elettaria cardamomum, are also known as organic cardamom seed or organic decorticated cardamom.
Cardamom is a firm, unripe dry fruit that contains about a dozen small, black-brown triangular seeds. When dried, the fruit looks like a papery pod, and while the pod carries some flavor it is fibrous and difficult to eat. Most often, recipes call for the whole or ground seeds rather than the full pod. It is often referred to as the "queen of spices"—black pepper is the king—and is considered the world's third most expensive spice behind saffron and vanilla.
Organic Cardamom Seeds are popular with manufacturers of coffee, tea, chai, chocolate, and pastries; and Middle Eastern restaurants.
We also carry Organic Ground Cardamom, and conventional Cardamom Seeds, Ground Cardamom, and Cardamom Pods.

Flavor Profile
Organic Cardamom Seeds have a complex flavor that combines citrus and mint with floral and eucalyptus notes, and a touch of pepper.

How To Use
Grind Organic Cardamom Seeds into a sweet and easy breakfast Chai Spiced Overnight Oats. Braise pears in cardamom syrup, or swap into the mix when making the Easiest Pancakes Ever. Boost fragrance and flavor in Butter Chicken with an extra pinch of cardamom. Pair with eggplant when making savory roasted Imam Bayildi, or make it sweet and enjoy cardamom-filled Apple Pie French Toast Casserole. Or steep with black tea for a soothing Masala Chai.
Use Organic Cardamom Seeds when making curries, DIY spice blends, rice dishes, mulled wine and cider, brewing, with chicken, lamb, fish, or pork, and when grilling, roasting, and baking.
Organic Cardamom Seeds work well in combination with caraway, chili powder, cinnamon, coriander, cumin, ginger, paprika, cilantro, garlic, orange, lemon, maple, and pepper.

Flavor Profile
Pungent, with a biting heat.

Heat Level

How to Use
Cayenne Chiles have long been the chile of choice in most Louisiana-style hot sauces. Add it to your dusting flour for fried chicken. Sprinkle over fish and vegetables. Organic Chipotle Flakes, Capsicum annuum, are hot chipotle morita chile flakes. They are also referred to as organic chipotle pepper flakes, organic smoky chipotle chili flakes, or organic chipotle chile flakes.

They are thick-walled chiles so once they are picked they are often smoked. Smoking preserves them more successfully than simply drying them, since the thicker walls take longer to dry and are more susceptible to microbial incursion.
Organic Chipotle Flakes are perfect for:
sauce, salsa, chile oil, chile paste, dip mix, jerky, and meal kit manufacturers;
Mexican, Latin American, BBQ, ramen, and Caribbean restaurants;
food trucks;
butchers;
meat processors;
seasoning companies; and
independent spice shops

Flavor Profile
Organic Chipotle Flakes are fruity and smoky, with notes of berries and chocolate.

How To Use

Spice up mushrooms with Champinones Al Ajillo Spanish Garlic Mushrooms. This flakes give Oaxacan Guacamole heat and depth. Toss with walnuts and spices for Sweet Chipotle Mixed Nuts, or dust over Sweet Potato Chili Fries.
Organic Chipotle Morita Chile Powder is versatile. It is excellent with grilled or roasted meats, in salsas, sauces, and stews, soups, or pasta, and with cheese, rice, potatoes, and roasted vegetables.
Organic Chipotle Morita Chile Powder pairs well with onion, garlic, coffee, chocolate, stone fruits, citrus, cilantro, sesame, cumin, coriander, thyme, tomato, and Mexican oregano.

instruction: Write a product description in the Spices, Inc. brand voice for the following spice.
input:
Name: Organic Coriander Seed
Category: Staple Spices
Characteristics: Organic
output:
Organic Coriander Seed, Coriandrum sativum L, is also called organic coriander seeds, organic bulk coriander or wholesale organic coriander.
The coriander plant is one of the few plants that produces both an herb and a spice; the dried fruit of the plant produces coriander seed, while the herb, cilantro, comes from the plant's leaves.
Businesses that frequently purchase Organic Coriander Seed are Indian and seafood restaurants; brewpubs; and companies that manufacture dog food, dietary pet supplements, and dog treats.
We also carry Organic Ground Coriander, and conventional Coriander Seeds, Indian Coriander Seeds, and Ground Coriander.

Flavor Profile
Organic Coriander Seed is sweet, nutty, warm and herbal with notes of citrus.

How To Use
Organic Coriander Seed can be swapped in to any recipe that calls for conventional coriander. You can use to make an organic version of Cincinnati Skyline Chili or Flat Iron Steak and Carrots with Parsley Pesto. It gives a fruity lift to Albondigas, a Spanish tapas-style beef meatball. Enjoy it in a hearty vegetarian Vegetable Jalfrezi. It is an aromatic standard in a classic Mexican Mole Sauce. Toast Organic Coriander Seed before using and make a richly-seasoned Punjabi Chicken with Tomatoes & Spinach.
Coriander is a great complement to lentils, beans, potatoes, rice, coconut milk, vegetables, fish, chicken, beef, chili, sausage, butter, fruits, and pickles.
Pair Organic Coriander Seed with onions, coconut, ginger, garlic, paprika, chile peppers, chocolate, lemon, orange, lime, tamarind, and sumac.

instruction: Write a product description in the Spices, Inc. brand voice for the following spice.
input:
Name: Organic Cracked Rosemary
Category: Culinary Herbs
Characteristics: Organic, White Label Products
output:
Organic Cracked Rosemary, Rosmarinus officinalis, is also called organic rosemary leaves, organic rosemary, or organic dried rosemary. It has an essential oil content of .5% to 2.5%.
The three most common “cuts” of rosemary are whole, cracked, and ground. Organic Cracked Rosemary is whole rosemary that has been ground to reduce the one-inch needles into smaller pieces. Whole needles can be hard, pointy, and difficult to work with. Cracked rosemary is better to use in blends, and has a shorter cooking time. We also carry conventional Cracked Rosemary, and conventional Ground Rosemary.
Organic Cracked Rosemary is popular with:
seasoning companies;
independent spice shops;
olive oil shops;
barbecue and hotel restaurants;
gluten-free bread and flour manufacturers; and
distillers

Organic Cracked Rosemary tastes cooling, woody, minty, and balsamic.

How To Use
Organic Cracked Rosemary adds and herbaceous bouquet to Provencal Chicken. It easily elevates comfort foods like Honey Mustard Potato Salad. Toss Organic Cracked Rosemary in your next party nut mix and enjoy Hill Country Spiced Pecans. It dresses up Garlic and Herb Mushrooms, and complements the sweet, savory heartiness of Sweet Apple Chicken Sausage and Roasted Vegetables.
Organic Cracked Rosemary is delicious with beef, chicken, fish, lamb, pork, veal, and wild game. Use in pot roasts, stews, stuffings, potatoes, tomatoes, eggplant, marinades, vinegars, breads, and sausages. It pairs well with wine, honey, garlic, chiles, olive oil, lemon, cinnamon, and cloves.

instruction: Write a product description in the Spices, Inc. brand voice for the following spice.
input:
Name: Organic Crushed Red Pepper Flakes
Category: Chiles
Characteristics: Chile Flakes, Classic Chili Spices, Organic, White Label Products
output:
Organic Crushed Red Pepper Flakes, Capsicum annuum, are also called organic red pepper flakes, organic crushed red pepper, or organic chili flakes. Our Organic Crushed Red Pepper Flakes are valued for their heat more than for their flavor, adding a sharp bite to dishes from around the world.
These flakes come from several types of chile peppers that fall into the desired heat range. Once the peppers are picked, the whole pepper is dried and pulverized, which includes the outer skins, veins, and seeds.
Organic Crushed Red Pepper Flakes are popular with seasoning companies, pickling, fermenting, condiments, cheese, and keto, paleo, and vegan manufacturers, food trucks, healthy, vegan, and Mediterranean restaurants, and spice and olive oil shops.

Flavor Profile
Organic Crushed Red Pepper Flakes taste hot with a sharp, biting flavor.

Heat Level
Organic Crushed Red Pepper Flakes are hot, measuring 30,000 – 40,000 SHU (Scoville Heat Units).

How To Use
Organic Crushed Red Pepper Flakes provide a nice liveliness to a variety of cuisines. They are excellent in chilis and chowders like this Crab and Corn Chowder. Add heat to creamy dishes by stirring it into this Spicy Coconut Shrimp. Fire up some Broccoli and Sun-Dried Tomato Pasta with a sprinkling of Organic Crushed Red Pepper Flakes. Or put this in the marinade to boost the spiciness of Sichuan Cornish Hens.
Red pepper flakes pair well with most spices, lemon juice, lime juice and coconut milk. Because they're typically a member of the nightshade family, they work well in combination with potatoes and tomatoes. Use Organic Crushed Red Pepper Flakes to add zest to chili, chowders, pickling, salads, homemade sausage, sandwiches, soups, spaghetti sauce, stir-fries, or vegetable recipes.

instruction: Write a product description in the Spices, Inc. brand voice for the following spice.
input:
Name: Organic Cumin Seed  
Category: Staple Spices
Characteristics: Kosher, Organic, White Label Products
output:
Organic Cumin Seed, Cuminum cyminum, is also known as organic cumin seeds, organic jeera or jeera seeds.
Cumin is a member of the Apiaceae family of plants and so, is a relative of fragrant spices and herbs like Caraway Seed, Dill Seed, and Dried Parsley.
Cumin has only been embraced by the US food scene in the last few decades but worldwide, it is one of the most consumed spices, right behind chiles and pepper.
Businesses that frequently purchase Organ Cumin Seed are American restaurants; seasoning companies; independent spice shops; butchers; meat processors; and companies that manufacture supplements.
We also have Organic Ground Cumin, conventional Cumin Seed, and conventional Ground Cumin available.

Flavor Profile
Organic Cumin Seed is warm, earthy, and nutty, with a hint of lemon

How To Use
Try Organic Cumin Seed in Sweet Chickpea Chili in Slow Cooker for a healthy, meatless main dish. Add it to sofrito, the Latin American seasoning base, and you’re on your way to an authentic carne asada. We suggest it in Arroz Con Pollo for an easy one-pot dish that can be made ahead and in large batches. Organic Cumin Seeds go well in meat dishes; add some to Moorish Pork Skewers or Smothered Chicken Burritos. Mix into Albondigas, the Spanish-style meatball. They are terrific with eggplant; add to the spice mix when making the eggplant dish Imam Bayildi, or add cumin-scented baba ghanoush to your appetizer menu.
Dry-roasting Organic Cumin Seed wakes up the volatile oils and unleashes a more intense aroma. Toast seeds and grind them in a mortar and pestle or a reserved spice grinder for bold flavor.
Organic Cumin Seeds pair with allspice, anise seed, brown mustard, cardamom, cinnamon, coriander, fennel, fenugreek, garlic, ginger, nutmeg, paprika, turmeric, and yellow mustard.

instruction: Write a product description in the Spices, Inc. brand voice for the following blend.
input:
Name: Organic Everything Bagel Seasoning
Category: Seasoning Blends
Cuisine: American
Characteristics: Organic Seasonings, White Label Products
Ingredients: organic garlic, kosher salt, organic poppy, organic onion, organic sesame seeds
output:
Bagels are one of the most popular food products around the world, easily adapted into many cuisines globally. With humble origins as a Jewish food product, the bagel has transformed into one of the symbols of New York City, as well as a classic component to a full breakfast spread.
Our Organic Everything Bagel Seasoning is sure to please and remind you of those homey mornings where you got up late and lazy only to pop a bagel into the toaster and then curl up on the couch to enjoy it under a sea of blankets.

Contents Hide
The Story of Organic Everything Bagel Seasoning
What's in it?
Flavor Profile
Where to Use
Helpful Hints
Read More

The Story of Organic Everything Bagel Seasoning
Bagels in general have an air of mystery surrounding their invention, but the everything bagel is the most mysterious of all. It was apparently the invention of a fifteen-year-old boy working in a bakery in the 1980s. While the story has not really been contested, it's never been proven either.
Either way, everything bagels exploded onto the scene and gained popularity in the United States rapidly, with their popularity never waning. Instead, this bagel became one of the defining foods of one of the most popular cities in the world, New York City. As some have said, when you think of foods that define New York City, thinking of everything bagels is one of your better options. This flavor was even one of the trending flavors in food culture in the United States in 2016. There was even an everything bagel flavored potato chip just recently!
Our conventional version of this everything bagel seasoning is super flavorful and quite popular, so we wanted to be sure we had an organic selection available for anyone who wants to enjoy this classic flavor organically. It was an easy choice to get working on this seasoning blend, as our conventional version was a near instant hit. As our selection of organic spices grows, we like to keep our organic seasoning blend selection growing, too.

What's in it?

Our Organic Everything Bagel Seasoning is hand blended with organic garlic, kosher salt, organic poppy, organic onion, and organic sesame.

Flavor Profile

Our Organic Everything Bagel Seasoning is has a nice savory garlic and onion flavor, with a wonderful crunch from the sesame and poppy seeds.

Where to Use

Use it on everything from homemade bagels to pasta. If you enjoy fettuccini alfredo, you can add some of this to the sauce for an intense, flavorful boost. It's so good with cheesy, creamy dishes, you could even put it in thick soups like cream of mushroom.
This seasoning blend is even great with cottage cheese. Take a heaping scoop of cottage cheese and add just a pinch or two of the organic everything bagel seasoning. The crunch from the seasoning blend is wonderful with the softer texture of the cheese, making for a fascinating flavor experience.
This blend is great with many different dishes, including smoked salmon or other fish dishes. It's even good on hot dogs! Put some in your bun before you add your hot dog and other toppings and be surprised by the lovely flavor this will add to the savory hot dog and sweeter bun.
A recipe we love to make with this seasoning blend is our Soft Pretzel recipe. The everything bagel flavor takes these pretzels to another level with zero effort from you. Just use this blend instead of a kosher salt to top the pretzels and voila.

Helpful Hints

Use less of this seasoning than you think you will need because it is extremely flavorful! It's easy to overdo it with this blend especially, since it is so delicious.

Organic Fennel Seed, Foeniculum vulgare, is also known as organic fennel seeds bulk, fennels seeds, bitter fennel fruit, Shamar seeds, or Shamar spice. It has a minimum volatile oil content of 1%.
Organic Fennel Seed is a member of the parsley family and is closely related to anise, asafoetida, caraway, chervil, coriander, cilantro, dill, cumin, and parsley. While the fennel’s seeds are considered a spice, the edible roots, stalks, and leaves of the plant are considered an herb.
Organic Fennel Seed is popular with:
American, pizza, and sandwich restaurants;
brewpubs;
butcher shops;
independent spice shops;
oil and jam manufacturers; and
catering companies
We also have Organic Ground Fennel and an assortment of conventional Fennel Seed products available.

Flavor Profile
Organic Fennel Seed has a warm, anise-licorice flavor with a camphoraceous undertone.

How To Use
Organic Fennel Seed is a common spice in the Mediterranean and European regions. French and Italian cooks often call fennel "the fish herb.” Try adding it to the breading when making Herb Crusted Tilapia. It would be a fragrant addition to Chicken Pho Soup. We added Organic Fennel Seed to Beef and Zucchini Parmigiana because its bright flavor adds contrast to the heavier flavor of beef. Grind them in the savory and sweet Indonesian condiment Kecap Manis.
Pair Organic Fennel Seeds with garlic, ginger, oregano, lemon, orange, clove, cinnamon, cheese, butter, and black pepper.
Organic Fennel Seeds is a good choice when making beets, sausage, lentils, potatoes, in sauerkraut, stews, meat and chicken dishes, sauces, herb butters, dips and dressings, salads, omelets, apple pie, cakes, pastries, puddings, and spiced fruit.

input:

Category: Seasoning Blends
Cuisine: Indian Seasonings
Characteristics: Organic Seasonings, Salt Free, White Label Products
Ingredients: organic turmeric, organic cinnamon, organic black pepper, organic ginger
output:
Organic Golden Milk is a salt-free, sugar-free, MSG-free, fully organic beverage blend that’s surprisingly versatile. It is also known as haldi doodh, organic golden milk powder, golden milk, golden milk powder, or golden milk mix.
Named for its golden color that is derived from turmeric, golden milk has terrific visual appeal as well as a bold, spicy flavor. When mixed with steaming, frothy plant-based or animal-based milk, it has the same soothing sentimentality that comes with a cup of hot milk. It can be enjoyed hot or cold, or in a variety of applications.
Organic Golden Milk is regularly purchased by independent spice shops; olive oil shops; seasoning companies; coffee, tea, and hemp product manufacturers; coffee shops; and healthy, vegan, or organic-focused restaurants.

Flavor Profile
Organic Golden Milk is earthy, warming, and spicy, with notes of pine, citrus, and sweet, woodsy cinnamon.

How To Use
Use our Organic Golden Milk blend to make a cup of Golden Milk; be sure to add a teaspoon of vanilla extract if you want it a little sweeter. This is a surprisingly versatile blend. Swap it in as the seasoning base for Roasted Carrot Soup or Butternut Squash Soup. Marinate chicken with yogurt and Organic Golden Milk and make zingy Indian Fried Chicken. It can be the main seasoning blend in Quick and Easy Vegetable Curry. Try this in something sweet, like spiced shortbread cookies, or give Healthy Carrot Cake Squares a kick.
Use in hot and cold milk-based beverages, teas, and coffees. Blend into ice cream, use in the topping for streusels, fruit crisps, or crumbles over coffee cakes or muffins. Add to curries, stir fries, fried foods, soups, stews, marinades, and dressings.

instruction: Write a product description in the Spices, Inc. brand voice for the following blend.
input:
Name: Organic Greek Seasoning
Category: Seasoning Blends
Cuisine: Mediterranean
Characteristics: Organic Seasonings, White Label Products
Ingredients: organic garlic, organic nutmeg, organic parsley, organic cinnamon, organic onion, organic oregano, organic black pepper, sea salt
output:
If you can't afford a vacation to the Mediterranean, this seasoning blend can transport you there for much cheaper, if only briefly. Through the experience of eating delicious food topped with Organic Greek Seasoning, you will find yourself immersed in the flavors of this delicious country.

Contents Hide
The Story of Organic Greek Seasoning
What's in it?
Flavor Profile
Where to Use
Helpful Hints
Read More

The Story of Organic Greek Seasoning
Each ingredient in this blend has some history within Greece. In Ancient Greece, people wore parsley as a garland to prevent drunkenness. Oregano grows wildly in Greece and has always been a part of their cuisine. Onion and garlic became a staple part of the Greek diet over time and has continued to help make it one of the Mediterranean's most flavorful cuisines. Cinnamon and nutmeg came from India and were rapidly adopted as an important part of the cuisine. Black pepper was of course one of the most sought-after spices in the history of the spice world, and this was no different in Greece.
Greek cuisine is full of fish, vegetables, grains, meat, wine, and of course plenty of olive oil. This blend complements all of these foods nicely and was developed as an organic version of our popular contemporary version. The more organics we get in, the more blends we are hoping to create to be able to keep up with the desires of customers who want their organic meals to taste just as delicious as they would if they were non-organic. It is easy to incorporate such flavorful blends into our lineup, especially when there is so much culture and food to be had from a Greek origin.

What's in it?

This is hand blended from Organic Mediterranean Oregano, Organic Onion Powder, Organic Garlic Powder, Organic Sea Salt, Organic Black Pepper, Organic Parsley, Organic Korintje Cinnamon, and Organic Ground Nutmeg.

Flavor Profile

This is a blend that is herbaceous and slightly sweet, with a tiny bit of bite from the black pepper.

Where to Use

You can use this seasoning blend on a variety of foods, from the meat end of the spectrum all the way to the vegetable end.
Organic Greek Seasoning is great to make sauce for gyros. It also makes an incredible marinade for Mediterranean style chicken, beef, lamb, pork, or fish. Any grilled food, shish-ke-bobs especially, taste excellent with this seasoning blend as a partner.
If you want to make your own gyros sauce, an easy recipe is to mix 2 cups of plain Greek yogurt, 1/4 cup chopped cucumber, 2 tablespoons of diced onion and 2 tablespoons of our Greek Seasoning. Greek yogurt is the yogurt of choice here because it is packed with protein and gives an authentic flavor, but you could substitute another plain yogurt if you so desire. Just keep in mind that it will not be nearly as thick as it would be with Greek yogurt.
A simple recipe for a meat marinade is 2 tablespoons Greek Seasoning, 2 tablespoons of olive oil, 2 tablespoons lemon juice and 1 tablespoon of warm water. This is a good amount for about a pound of meat. Place your meat in a large re-sealable plastic bag and be sure that your meat is covered evenly with the marinade. Leave the marinating meat in the refrigerator for 8-12 hours before cooking.
Greek seasoning is also incredible on popcorn, roasted vegetables, and on pasta topped with a little olive oil.

Helpful Hints

This Organic Greek Seasoning can be used in all the same ways that you would use conventional Greek seasoning!

instruction: Write a product description in the Spices, Inc. brand voice for the following spice.
input:
Name: Organic Green Jalapeno Chile Powder
Characteristics: Chile Powders, Organic, White Label Products
output:
Organic Green Jalapeño Chile Powder, Capsicum annuum, measures 2,500-8,000 Scoville Heat Units (SHU). It is also known as organic jalapeño powder or bulk organic jalapeño powder.
Jalapeños are widely considered to be the most recognized chile in the US. They are one of the first and oldest cultivated crops in the Western Hemisphere, as they were in cultivation even before the Aztec civilization, which thrived from 1345-1521.
Organic Green Jalapeño Chile Powder is popular with food trucks, taco restaurants, and olive oil and spice shops.
We also have a conventional Jalapeno Powder or dried Jalapeno Flakes available.

Flavor Profile
Organic Green Jalapeño Chile Powder has an earthy-grassy flavor with a sharp heat.

Heat Level
Jalapeños are considered a medium heat chile, measuring between 2,500 and 8,000 SHU (Scoville Heat Units).

How To Use
Add this to your favorite seasoning blend or custom blend to create a variety of Mexican and Tex-Mex dishes. Stir into Enmoladas to boost the heat. This will go beautifully in Black Bean and Corn Salsa. Blend into the seasoning for Jackfruit Tacos. It’s great in chili, so add Organic Green Jalapeno Chile Powder to Mexican Chicken Chili or Green Chile Stew. Smash into Oaxacan Guacamole. Mix with sugar and toss over popcorn, or stir it into your favorite barbecue rub for a fun kick.
Our Organic Green Jalapeño Chile Powder can be added to chili, corn bread, salsa, sauces, spice blends, stews, and taco meat. It adds an excellent kick to chicken, pork, seafood, eggs, and popcorn.

instruction: Write a product description in the Spices, Inc. brand voice for the following spice.
input:
Name: Organic Ground Allspice
Category: Baking
Characteristics: Beer Brewing, Organic, White Label Products
output:
Organic Ground Allspice, Pimenta dioica, is also called organic allspice, ground organic allspice, or organic allspice powder. It has an essential oil content between 1.5% and 5%.
Allspice was discovered on the island of Jamaica by Columbus during his second voyage to the New World in 1494. Columbus called Allspice “pimiento,” which is what the Spanish called black peppercorns because the dried Allspice berries looked similar to large, smooth, brownish black peppercorns.
Organic Ground Allspice is popular with:
sauce and supplement manufacturers;
coffee shops;
seasoning companies; and
specialty spice shops
We also carry Organic Allspice Berries, Allspice Berries, Jamaican Allspice Berries, Ground Jamaican Allspice, and Ground Allspice.
One teaspoon of Organic Ground Allspice is approximately equal to five whole allspice berries.

Flavor Profile
Organic Ground Allspice tastes warm, sweet, and peppery with floral undertones.

How To Use
Use Organic Ground Allspice to flavor vegetables like carrots, parsnips, sweet potatoes, turnips, and winter squash. It adds a dimension to chicken, tomato, and vegetable soups and stews like Mexican birria. Blend into relishes, gravies, and meat marinades. It is an indispensable ingredient for gingerbread, but can be also added to a variety of desserts like apple or pumpkin pie, fruit compote, and rice pudding.
Organic Ground Allspice is perfect to use for grilled or roasted meats and vegetables, puddings, desserts, baked goods, marinades, chilis, dressings, soups, stews, and marinades.
Allspice works well in combination with chili powder, cloves, coriander, garlic, ginger, mustard, pepper, rosemary and thyme.

instruction: Write a product description in the Spices, Inc. brand voice for the following spice.
input:
Name: Organic Ground Black Pepper Medium Grind 
Category: Staple Spices
Characteristics: Organic, Kosher, Pepper, White Label Products
output:
Organic Ground Black Pepper Medium Grind is the fruit of the Piper nigrum plant. It is also referred to as organic medium black pepper.
Pepper is a berry, complete with a skin, a fruity layer, and a single inner seed. Its heat comes from piperine, an alkyloid compound found in both the outer fruit layer and the seed. The outer fruit layer also contains terpenes (pronounced "tur peans"), which provide the instantly recognizable citrusy, floral and woody notes. A good quality black pepper contains between 4.6% and 9.7% piperine, and between 1% and 2.5% essential oils.
Businesses that frequently purchase Organic Ground Black Pepper Medium Grind are:
independent spice shops;
seasoning companies;
taco food trucks;
delis;
healthy and vegan restaurants; and
companies that manufacture jams, vegan cheeses, and dog food
Please visit our pepper page to browse our full selection of pepper products available.

Flavor Profile
Organic Ground Black Pepper Medium Grind delivers a clean heat with notes of pine and warm, lemony undertones.

How To Use
Use Organic Black Pepper Medium Grind as you would any other kind of pepper. This globally adored spice goes well in everything from roasts and casseroles to salads and even can be a surprise ingredient in desserts. It can be added at the beginning or at the end of cooking time; longer cooking time will mellow the bite of the pepper, but its woodsy nuances will permeate the dish. Short or no cooking time will deliver a more aggressive pepper flavor.
Organic Black Pepper Medium Grind can be found in just about every dish, but it works particularly well in combination with basil, cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, coriander, cumin, garlic, ginger, nutmeg, parsley, rosemary, thyme and turmeric. It is also good with chicken, eggs, fish, pork, salads, soup, strawberries, and tomatoes.

Organic Ground Cardamom, Elettaria cardamomum, is the brownish-white powder that comes from grinding cardamom seeds. It is also known as organic ground cardamon, ground cardamon, ground cardamom organic or organic cardamom ground.
Ground Cardamom comes from firm, unripened cardamom fruit, or pods, that contain about a dozen seeds each. It is a member of the Zinziberaceae, or ginger, family, and is closely related to galangal, ginger, grains of paradise, and turmeric.
Organic Ground Cardamom is regularly purchased by:
health and wellness-adjacent food manufacturers;
coffee or tea manufacturers;
brewpubs and distilleries;
coffee shop restaurants;
bakeries; and
cafes
We also carry Organic Cardamom Seeds and conventional cardamom products like Ground Cardamom and Cardamom Seeds.

Flavor Profile
Organic Ground Cardamom’s complex flavor is slightly floral, sweet and spicy with citrusy notes.

How To Use
Organic Ground Cardamom plays a starring role in Southeast Asian curries, desserts and pilafs. Add it to Vindaloo Curry Spiced Bean and Tomato Soup or Butter Chicken for extra aroma and indefinable flavor. Stir into chicken for a savory Chicken Tagine, or add to a marinade for lamb chops with garlic and pepper, and grill. Or try its softer side; make a sweet and easy breakfast Chai Spiced Overnight Oats. Braise pears in cardamom syrup, or swap into the Easiest Pancakes Ever. Add some to snickerdoodles, French toast, or rice pudding for a new take on some old classics.
Cardamom works well in combination with yogurt, fruit, chicken, grilled lamb, meatballs, pastries, sausage, oats, beans, apples, and almonds.
Pair Organic Ground Cardamom with black pepper, saffron, butter, parsley, cilantro, clove, cinnamon, coriander, cumin, ginger, paprika, and citrus flavors like lemon and orange.

instruction: Write a product description in the Spices, Inc. brand voice for the following spice.
input:

Category: Staple Spices
Characteristics: Organic, White Label Products
output:
Organic Ground Celery Seed, Apium graveolens, is an organic spice that is also known as organic ground celery or organic bulk ground celery.
Celery is from the family Apiaceae, or the parsley family. Other members of this family include dill, chervil, anise, fennel, cumin, caraway, and coriander. Celery seeds are technically considered the fruit of the celery plant, and are so small that it takes more than 45,000 of them to yield one ounce of product.
Organic Ground Celery Seed is popular with manufacturers of meal mixtures, mixes, packaged meat and bread; Mediterranean restaurants; independent spice shops; olive oil shops; and seasoning companies.
We also have Organic Celery Seeds and conventional Celery Seed and Ground Celery Seed available.
One teaspoon of Organic Ground Celery Seed equals 2 Tablespoons minced celery.

Flavor Profile
Organic Ground Celery Seed has a hay-like, grassy, slightly bitter taste and aroma.

How to Use
Organic Ground Celery Seed can be used in a variety of dishes. It is essential in Best Dry Rub for Ribs or any barbeque rub recipe. Organic Ground Celery Seed is a must-have in deviled eggs and macaroni salad. Organic Ground Celery Seed can easily be used as a substitute for fresh celery in Easy Chicken Pot Pie, Vegetarian Gumbo with Vegan Andouille Meatballs, Red Beans and Rice and in Creole Sausage and Peppers.
Use the distinctive, pungent flavor of celery seeds in your bread, brine recipes, casseroles, chicken soup, coleslaw, eggs, meat, pickles, vegetable dishes, gravies, salad dressings, sauces, sauerkraut, stuffing, stews and fresh tomato juice. Organic Ground Celery seeds also work well in combination with salt, onion, bell peppers, carrots, turmeric, chicken, sage, cumin, soy sauce, ginger, and vinegar.

instruction: Write a product description in the Spices, Inc. brand voice for the following spice.
input:
Name: Organic Ground Cloves
Category: Baking
Characteristics: Organic, White Label Products
output:
Organic Ground Cloves,Syzygium aromaticum, are also known as organic bulk ground cloves. Cloves are a pungent spice, delivering a minimum of 10% essential oil by weight.
Cloves are the unopened buds of an Indonesian evergreen tree. The buds turn red right before they open, which is when they are harvested and dried. The word “clove” comes from the Latin clavus, or nail, and European colonizers named them so because of their spiky appearance.
Organic Ground Cloves are popular with seasoning companies; honey, sauce, and baked goods manufacturers; independent spice shops; Mexican and African restaurants; delis; and breweries.
We also have conventional Ground Cloves and Whole Cloves available.

Flavor Profile
Organic Ground Cloves are peppery, woodsy, and intensely warm, with a mild, numbing quality.

How To Use
Organic Ground Cloves are used in popular soups such as red lentil soup and Spicy Pumpkin Soup. Substitute Organic Ground Cloves into Apple Pie Fries or Healthy Carrot Cake Squares. Organic Ground Cloves can spice up Cincinnati Skyline Chili and Birria – Mexican Beef Stew, the latter of which can even be shredded into tacos. Use this when making an organic DIY Dry Rib Rub.
Organic Ground Cloves are delicious in savory or sweet pies and puddings, dessert cakes, candies, or cookies. Add to gravies, cranberry sauce, roasts, applesauce, tea, cider, BBQ sauce, chili, soups, stews, and braises.
Organic Ground Cloves pair well with cinnamon, allspice, vanilla, onion, citrus peel, star anise, basil, pork, ham, beef, turkey, peppercorns, oranges, carrots, apples, beets, and pumpkin.

input:
Name: Organic Ground Coriander

output:
The pungent flavor of Organic Ground Cumin is earthy and nutty with warming aromas and just a touch of an herbal lemon essence to finish. Our Organic Ground Cumin provides a distinctive flavor that has been part of the spice trade for thousands of years. A close relative of fragrant fennel and caraway, cumin is native to the Mediterranean region and northern Africa. It was used by the ancient Egyptians as a seasoning, as medicine, and in the mummification process, and has been referenced in the world’s oldest “cookbook”, the Yale culinary tablets, a collection of recipes on clay tablets that were written in Mesopotamia in roughly 1700 BCE.

Cumin has seen its reach grow across Asia and India, through the Caribbean, and down into Latin America. It is spicy, but not like the heat found in chile peppers. Its spice is more a perception of its intensity thanks to the high volatile oil content in the seeds. The volatile oils in cumin will dissipate quickly after the seeds are ground, so we grind cumin in smaller batches, several times a week. We also grind our cumin to a slightly coarse grind; the coarseness offers the volatile oils more of a seed to adhere to which slows the dissipation of the oils. This helps us provide our customers with the freshest spice possible.

Tips From Our Kitchen

In the cuisines of Asia, Latin America, the Caribbean, the Middle East and North Africa, cumin is a signature spice. Have a tagine on a bed of spiced couscous. Make enchiladas that have a deep, earthy flavor. The slow-cooked Cuban stew ropa vieja begins with cumin and other seasonings stirred into a rich base made from vegetables and the fond from browned beef. It is a key ingredient in various spice blends and many bean, couscous, curries, rice and vegetable dishes.

We do recommend that you use cumin sparingly at first, until you know how much you like, as its flavor is potent.

Our Organic Ground Cumin is cultivated in India.

This product is certified kosher.

instruction: Write a product description in the Spices, Inc. brand voice for the following spice.
input:
Name: Organic Ground Ginger  
Category: Baking
Characteristics: Kosher, Organic, Umami, White Label Products
output:
Organic Ground Ginger, Zingiber officinale, is an herbaceous perennial that belongs to the family Zingiberaceae. Other members of this family include Turmeric, Cardamom and Galangal. Both Ginger and Turmeric are a rhizome which are thick underground stems that sprout roots underground and shoots above.
While some botanists believe ginger is native to China, others argue that it is indigenous to India (the greatest genetic diversity of this species has been found on the eastern coast of India). Ginger has subsequently been cultivated in Southeastern Asia, Africa, Jamaica, India and Australia.
Ginger has 1% to 4% essential oil, depending on the variety. The essential oil is mainly comprised of sesquiterpenes, which gives the ginger its characteristic scent, but not its bite.
Ginger is called zanjabil in Arabic, gan jiang in Mandarin, gingembre in French, ingefer in German, sauth in Hindi, shoga in Japanese, gengibre in Portuguese, imibir in Russian, and jengibre in Spanish. East Indian Pepper or Ginger Powder are other names for ground ginger.

Contents Hide
History of Ginger
Ginger Cultivation
Cooking with Ginger
What Does Ginger Taste Like?
Substitutions and Conversions
Read More

History of Ginger
Ginger is from the 14th century Old English gingifer which comes from the Late Latin gingiber, derived from the Sanskrit singabera. Singabera means "shaped like a deer's antlers," which is a fitting description of ginger. It is one of the best known and oldest spices in the world. The Maharata, a Hindu text written around 4 BCE, recorded the use of ginger as an ingredient in stewed meat dishes. Other references to ginger appeared in the writings of Confucius (551-470 BC) and also in the Holy Qur'an (609-632 AD) where it is said to be one of the fruits found in heaven which await the righteous: "And they will be given to drink there of a cup (of wine) mixed with zanjabil". (Q. 76:17) Zanjabil is the Arabic word for Ginger.
Ginger's use in China and India dates back to ancient times, and in the 1st century AD traders introduced ginger to the Mediterranean region. As one of the spices first traded along the Spice routes and Silk Road, ginger's value held strong. Discordes, a Greek military physician, and Pliny, a Roman naturalist, valued ginger's power to solve a variety of complaints relating to digestion. Ginger was used primarily as a medicine in ancient Rome and Greece, but by the late middle ages in Europe it had gained considerable traction as a sweet and an aphrodisiac. By the 11th century ginger was well known in England. The Spanish Conquistadors brought it to Mexico and the West Indies. By the mid 1500's demand for this spice reached such high levels that both the Portuguese and Spanish were cultivating it in the new tropical colonies and exporting back into Europe.
Ginger's popularity in America came with the colonists. Having been previously very popular in Europe, ginger's presence in the New World was inevitable. Of course, they would take their spices with them to their new home. It was easy to cultivate on the newly colonized land, and then they would have had plenty to grind up. Ground was the most popular of all the forms of ginger. Today, thanks to the increased interest in Asian style cooking, fresh ginger has become more widely available in the United States and more popular in general. Ground ginger retains its popularity as well.
The very first American cookbook had three different recipes for gingerbread; not only was the type suitable for cookies included, but the kind used in breads was also there. Gingerbread cookies were sometimes used in bargaining with potential voters for their votes in early America- politicians would try to secure the public's positive opinion of them with the decadent, snappy cookies.
Ginger is frequently used as a palate cleanser between dishes or types of sushi in Asian restaurants.
According to WebMD, Ginger contains chemicals that may reduce nausea and inflammation. Researchers believe the chemicals work principally in the intestines and stomach, but they may also influence the brain and nervous system to control nausea.
A review of 6 randomized, double-blind, controlled trials with more than 650 participants, published in the April 2005 issue of the journal, Obstetrics and Gynecology suggests that ginger is effective in reducing the severity of nausea and vomiting in pregnant women. This research also did not find any significant adverse side effects during the monitored pregnancies.
The November 2003 issue of Life Sciences published a study suggesting that ginger's beneficial inflammation effects can be traced to one of its active chemical compounds, 6-gingerol (a relative of capsaicin and piperine). In this test tube study, 6-gingerol was found to significantly inhibit the production of nitric oxide, a highly reactive nitrogen molecule that quickly forms a very damaging free radical called peroxynitrite. Peroxynitrite generation is a crucial pathogenic mechanism in conditions such as cancer, diabetes, chronic heart failure, chronic inflammatory diseases, myocardial infarction, neurodegenerative disorders, circulatory shock and stroke.

Ginger Cultivation
Ginger's leafy stems grow more than 3 feet high with 6"-12" leaves. Ginger sprouts flowers that are in dense cone shaped spikes about 2"-3" long and 1" thick.Today, Ginger is almost never grown from seed and is instead propagated by planting rootstalk cuttings. To harvest, the ginger rhizomes are pulled from the soil, cleaned and then dried in the sun. The dried ginger rhizomes are irregular in shape, branched or palmate (having a shape similar to that of a hand with the fingers extended). The color varies from pale yellow brown to light brown to dark yellow. Ginger may be unpeeled (leaving the outer layer), partially peeled, or completely peeled (removing the outer skin and the thinner inner skin).The flavor and quality of dried ginger varies greatly depending on where it is cultivated. Jamaican ginger that is peeled is considered by ginger coinsurers as being the finest available. Ginger from Jamaica has a pale color, subtle aroma and very fine textured powder, it's also the most expensive and very difficult to find, as practically all the rhizomes grown on the island are consumed there. African grown ginger tends to be unpeeled and harsh, while Australian cultivated ginger has the strongest lemony undertones of all the gingers.Depending on the time of year, our Ginger is sourced from India, China, Jamaica or Nigeria.
Cooking with Ginger
Ground Ginger is a staple in bakers' pantries and is frequently used in combination with ingredients with strong flavors such as molasses.In the Middle East, ginger is used to season couscous, tangines and slow-cooked meat dishes made with fruit. Ginger plays a key role in Indian dishes, and is a signature ingredient in Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Vietnamese cuisines for flavoring meat, seafood and vegetarian dishes. In this country, ginger is probably most recognized as a baking spice in cakes and cookies.It is best to add Ground Ginger when the dish is almost finished cooking as it is easy to overcook which causes the flavor to quickly dissipate. If you are making something that is quite dry, dissolve the ginger powder in warm water or another warm liquid so that it can be evenly distributed in the dish.Pickled ginger is common in Japanese cuisine to clear the mouth of flavor between dishes, and is also eaten as a snack. In India and Sri Lanka, both dried and fresh gingers are frequently consumed. Dried, it is found in curry blends and snacks, stir frys, or desserts. Indian vegetarians love to use this spice to give a lot of flavor to many of their dishes.Ginger pairs nicely with carrots, pumpkin, winter squashes and sweet potatoes. Ginger also blends exceptionally well with fruits such as bananas, pears, pineapples and oranges.Ginger flourishes when used in combination with cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, dried fruits, honey, nutmeg, nuts, preserved lemons, paprika, pepper and saffron.Some of the our more popular recipes with ground ginger are Punjabi Chicken with Tomatoes and Spinach, Sichuan Pepper and Beef Stir Fry, Ginger Spiced Grilled Pork Chops, and Moroccan Soup.We also carry Crystallized Ginger (also known as Candied Ginger or Glace Ginger) and a conventional Ginger Powder, or ground ginger.While fresh ginger tends to be much less expensive than ground ginger, you don't need near as much ground ginger in recipes and ground ginger lasts much longer than fresh.
What Does Ginger Taste Like?
Ground Organic Ginger is peppery and warm with lemon undertones. You'll also notice a slightly fiery taste with a pungent aroma.
Substitutions and Conversions
Ginger can be replaced with ground allspice, ground cinnamon, ground mace, or ground nutmeg if it is not immediately on hand.
Fresh ginger is often less expensive than ground ginger, but the benefit of having ground ginger is that has a much longer shelf-life. You also need much less ground ginger in recipes than you would if you were using fresh ginger. 1 tablespoon of fresh ginger is roughly equal to 1/8 teaspoon of ground ginger.
Since they have two very distinct flavor profiles, we do not recommend substituting fresh ginger in any recipe that calls for ground ginger, or using ground ginger for any recipe that calls for fresh ginger.

output:
Organic Italian seasoning is a classic and certainly has a home in any kitchen cupboard that faces the possibility of a big pasta night. Perfect for lasagna, spaghetti, and pizza, this spice blend is a delicious nod to the wonderfully complex flavors of Italian cuisine.

Sometimes you will hear this being called Italian herb seasoning, Italian herb blend, or Italian seasoning mix, but those names only serve to denote the same blend that has become a tried and true spice blend addition to the American diet.

Contents Hide

The Story Behind the Seasoning

What's in Organic Italian Seasoning?

What's the Difference Between Italian Seasoning and Pizza Seasoning?

Flavor Profile

What Do You Use Italian Seasoning For?

The Story Behind the Seasoning

When thinking about spice cabinets all over America, Italian Seasoning is one that is sure to be found in almost every single one. With so many people turning towards organics for their food preparation, we decided that an organic option of this classic spice blend was necessary to have on hand. There are very few people that can say the scent of all the herbs and spices at an Italian restaurant don't automatically transport them to a mythical land of good food, fine wine, and unusually loud laughter. We decided we should incorporate something into our inventory that would provide for the organic crowd while also remaining familiar and delicious. Organic Italian Seasoning it was.

In authentic Italian cooking, one will usually find only one or two herbs called for, though occasionally you will see the need for a few more. This seasoning blend is perfect for those instances, or for when you feel like adding a little something extra to your old family sauce recipe.

What's in Organic Italian Seasoning?

Our Organic Italian Seasoning is made of Organic Rosemary, Organic Basil, Organic Mediterranean Oregano, Organic Sage and Organic Marjoram. It is hand blended.

What's the Difference Between Italian Seasoning and Pizza Seasoning?

Italian seasoning is usually compromised of only different kinds of herbs, while pizza seasoning is usually herbs with some other ingredients like crushed red pepper and red bell peppers. These peppers are typically added to the blend because of the American tradition of spicing up pizza with red pepper flakes. Pizza seasoning is especially useful when eating a bland frozen pizza. It can transform the pizza from something less than flavorful to an enjoyable food eating experience.

Flavor Profile

Our Organic Italian Seasoning has a mellow, rich, savory herbal flavor.

What Do You Use Italian Seasoning For?

This spice blend can be used in any pasta dish to enhance the flavor immensely. The lovely herbal notes will provide a more robust flavor to any pasta dish, particularly if it has a tomato based sauce.

Mix this blend in with some olive oil for dipping bread. When baking chicken, first coat it in an olive oil and Organic Italian Seasoning blend mixture and proceed. The result will be a deliciously herbal tasting chicken. You can use it on meats before grilling for a similarly subtle herbaceous flavor.

It is excellent when mixed with butter, garlic, and parmesan for a delicious garlic bread spread.

This blend tastes incredible on vegetables like potatoes, carrots, squash, or eggplants. Mushrooms are delicious with these flavors as well. Try frying some up in olive oil and adding some of this blend to them just as they are about to be pulled from the heat. The flavor will permeate without disappearing completely, which is common in cooking if the herbs are added too early. Sprinkle some Sazon Seasoning on them to finish it all off while creating a delightful Latin American/ Mediterranean fusion dish.

A good recipe for how to make an easy Italian dressing is to add three tablespoons of organic Italian seasoning, a half tablespoon of red pepper flakes, two cloves of chopped garlic, and a squeeze of fresh lemon juice to a half cup of olive oil. Stir them up and you'll have a lovely, light dressing that can take the place of any store-bought dressing or used as a marinade for chicken. You could remove the red pepper flakes from the recipes if you wanted something less spicy.

Helpful Hints

Dumping a pound of this stuff on your lasagna certainly won't make you any more Italian than the day you were born. So, use a little at a time for that cozy flavor of a delicious dinner from your favorite local slice of Italy.

Use sparingly and add more to taste as you like. Our blends are very aromatic and flavorful, and this organic blend is no different in that regard.

We have a plethora of other blends that could fit in with Italian cuisine like Tuscany Bread Dipping Seasoning, Garlic and Herb, Pizza Seasoning, Naples Seasoning and Spaghetti Seasoning.

Some of our favorite recipes using Italian Seasoning are Aromatic Herbed Chicken, Italian Wedding Soup, Hot Italian Giardiniera, and Homemade Marinara and Creamy Polenta. The conventional blend mentioned in all of these recipes can be easily substituted for the Organic blend.

Organic Mediterranean Oregano, Origanum vulgare, is a member of the Lamiaceae, or mint, family. Other members of this family include basil, lavender, marjoram, mint, rosemary, sage, savory, and thyme. Our bulk organic oregano is also referred to as organic oregano and organic dried oregano.

Mediterranean Oregano has an essential oil composition of about 1.0% to 2%, which accounts for its strong, peppery flavor. The word oregano is derived from the Greek origanon, which comes from combination of the word oros, or "mountain" and ganos which means "brightness" or "joy". The Greeks believed that the Goddess Aphrodite created oregano, as she wanted it to represent a symbol of joy growing in her garden.

This herb is popular with seasoning companies, gourmet condiment and dressing manufacturers, brewpub and Mediterranean restaurants, and spice and olive oil shops.

Flavor Profile

Organic Mediterranean Oregano is woodsy and peppery, with an astringent bite and notes of pine, lemon, and camphor.

How To Use

Oregano is a versatile herb that plays a starring role in Egyptian, Greek, Italian, Lebanese, Mediterranean, Palestinian, Philippine, Portuguese, Spanish, Syrian and Turkish cuisines. It adds depth to Grilled Vegetable Pasta or any kind of baked, cheesy Parmigiana dish. Add some to Sambousek, a traditional Egyptian street food. It adds to the herbaceous freshness of Provencal Chicken and also dresses up the crunchy crust in Herb-Crusted Tilapia. Use in the marinade for Moorish Pork Skewers. It’s also a great addition to a potluck standard, the 4-Bean Salad.

Use Organic Mediterranean Oregano with cream sauces, vinegars, salad dressings, soups, and herb butters. It is also outstanding in egg and cheese dishes. Organic Mediterranean Oregano works well in combination with basil, garlic, thyme, and parsley. Organic New Mexico Red Chile Powder, Capsicum annuum, is a mild chile powder that measures between 1,000-2,500 Scoville Heat Units (SHU). It is also referred to as organic New Mexico red chili powder, New Mexico red chili powder or red chili powder.
Our Organic New Mexico Red Chile Powder is ground from chiles grown on a fourth-generation family farm that has been in operation since the early 1900s, in the famed Hatch region of New Mexico. Chile peppers from the Hatch region are renowned for their unique flavor, products of the area’s terroir—the hot days, cool nights, and rich, loamy soil of the area’s farmland. Chile peppers became a cultural institution about a hundred years ago when agribusiness farming began in earnest, though chiles have been grown in the area for about 500 years.
Organic New Mexico Red Chile Powder is popular with seasoning companies; brewpubs; taco food trucks; bar & grill, burger, and seafood restaurants; and independent spice shops.
We also have whole, dried Organic New Mexico Chiles as well as conventional New Mexico Chile Powder, New Mexico Red Chile Flakes, and New Mexico Chiles.
1 teaspoon of Organic New Mexico Red Chile Powder is approximately equal to 1 whole Organic New Mexico Chile.

Flavor Profile
Organic New Mexico Red Chile Powder has rich, raisiny notes with hints of cocoa and smokiness.

The Story of Our Organic Tuscany Blend
The Tuscany region of Italy, which has a reputation for beautiful art and an even bigger reputation for delicious bread, is home to some of the most flavorful food in the world. Italian meals tend to have a few courses, and bread is a typical appetizer. This is especially true in Tuscany. Here la dolce far niente, or the sweetness of doing nothing, is celebrated with good food and good wine. Lingering on a meal's flavors is one of the best parts of eating in this region, because unlike typical Americans, people from Tuscany enjoy a long, drawn out dinner. The foods of Tuscany are thought to be some of the healthiest and the least fatty of Italy. Unlike Americans who slather butter all over their bread, Italians prefer to spread olive oil over fresh bread which is either plain or seasoned with a menagerie of spices.
This bread dipping seasoning has all the classic Italian herbs, like rosemary and basil, but it also has the spicy, yet still classically Italian, red pepper flakes. We wanted to create an organic version of our most popular bread dipping seasoning blend and with our vast inventory of organic products, we were able to achieve this. This blend is zesty, savory, garlicky, and perfect for imagining what Italy might taste like, especially if you've never been.

What's in it?

Our Organic Tuscany is made from Coarse Sea Salt, Organic Garlic, Organic Black Pepper, Organic Onion, Organic Red Pepper Flakes, Organic Rosemary, Organic Basil, Organic Oregano, and Organic Parsley.

Flavor Profile

Where to Use it

Combine a half cup of olive oil and three tablespoons or so of this blend together and allow the mixture to sit for 20 to 30 minutes before enjoying with some fresh bread. This is enough dip for about two or three people to enjoy, so scale back or up depending on how many people are snacking. If you think the flavor of the dip is too intense, add some more oil to dilute it. Alternatively, if you think that there isn't enough flavor, add more Tuscany!
For a quick salad dressing or marinade for pork, chicken, or fish, combine 3 tablespoons of the bread dipping seasoning with 2/3 cups of olive oil and 1/3 cup red wine vinegar. This bright, fragrant dressing will liven up a boring salad. Throw some croutons on top for some extra texture and flavor.
Some recipes that use this blend as a seasoning instead of a marinade or dipping sauce are Caprese Salad, Tuscan Style Roasted Carrots, and Mediterranean Pitas.

It's got beautiful flavors, a garlicky, salty, herby, and savory blend full of potential. What goes better with a loaf of fresh baked bread and a saucer of oil and Organic Tuscany to dip it in? A bottle of wine. Some of our wine maker customers purchase our Tuscany for their specialty wine shops, encouraging you to purchase a bottle or two and some spices to take home for your favorite bread and wine snack. This blend is delicious on pasta as well, making it a staple for our customers make homemade pasta dishes to serve at their restaurants. There's nothing better than a Tuscany inspired blend and a plate full of pasta made from an Italian Nonna's recipe. Buying Organic Tuscany in bulk is wise because it is certain to fly of the shelves. Category: Baking

output:
Sesame seeds are just a small part of the history of food in the world, but they are by no means unimportant. Full of flavor and oil that has long been an essential tool for human life, these tiny seeds are scientifically called Sesamum indicum. The name sesame comes from a Greek word, "sesamon," and the sesame seed is a star ingredient in several global cuisines including Middle Eastern, Asian, African, and Mediterranean.

While there are no volatile oils in sesame seeds, they are made up of 45-65% fixed oil predominantly made up of olein.

Sesame is called "juljulan" by speakers of Arabic, "zi mah" to those who use Mandarin, "till" in French, "sesam" by German speakers, "gingili" or "til" in the Hindi language, "goma" in Japanese, "gergelim" to speakers of Portuguese, "kunzhut" in Russian, and finally "ajonjoli" in Spanish.

Contents Hide

History of White Sesame Seeds

Cooking with Organic White Sesame Seed

What Does Organic White Sesame Seed Taste Like?

History of White Sesame Seeds

Sesame seeds were one of the first condiments and one of the first plants to be used for edible oil. Of the historical records we have of white sesame seeds, those of the Assyrian people are of the first written records. They had tablets where they recorded stories, of which was one about how their gods drank sesame wine the night before they created the earth.

In Egypt, sesame seed is mentioned on the Ebers papyrus, a scroll of 65 feet in length that described ancient herbs and spices. It's considered one of the earliest medical texts, dated about 1550 BCE, with roughly 700 proposed remedies for afflictions like crocodile bites and ingrown toenail pain. There are also some mixtures listed to help rid your home of pests like insects, scorpions, and rats. Sesame oil was also one of the oils used to power Egyptian lamps, as evidence from several archeological sites shows.

In Hindu tradition, the sesame seed represents immortality. Women of ancient Babylon would mix honey and sesame seeds together to stave off the aging process and give their bodies more strength. They would also use sesame oils to create perfumes and medicines. The ancient Greeks and Romans believed the seed would give them strength to conquer new lands and territories.

Sesame seed was introduced to Europe in the first century, and in the 17th century it was introduced to the United States when African slaves brought their foods and traditions to them to the states during their forced relocation.

Organic White Sesame Seed Cultivation

The sesame plant is able to survive in several types of soils, but they prefer well-drained, organic material rich, pH neutral soil. It thrives in the climates found in India, China, Korea, Egypt, and East Africa. The plant is drought tolerant because of its extensive root system, and it will recognize warmer environments and extend its roots to suit that environment better before it will sprout. Seeds grow inside seed pods called "buns." The buns will burst when the seeds are fully ripe. Farmers tend to cut the buns from the plant before they are fully ripe because the pods tend to burst forth with enough force to spread the seeds out all over the place. This is good for the future of the plant, not so great for farmers who want to sell the seeds. When stored upright and allowed to finish ripening in a controlled environment, the seeds can be caught once the pods erupt. Sesame takes only 90 to 120 days to fully ripen, and the buns will shift from a green color to a yellowish-brown color when they are ripe. The plants may grow up to six feet tall.

Where is it From?

Our Organic White Sesame Seeds are grown in India.

Types of Sesame Seed

Despite the fact that sesame seeds all come from the same type of plant, their color is determined by both the environment they grew in and also the variety of that type of plant that they grow on. Seeds are categorized by colors. Black, brown, red, and white sesame seeds are the four distinct colors, but the lighter colored seeds are used most often in Western and Middle Eastern cuisines while the darker colors are more likely to be found in Asian cuisines.

Cooking with Organic White Sesame Seed

Popular in baking, sesame seeds are great for buns, bagels, or breads of all types. You can used them in honey, sauces, and dips to add a bit of nutty crunch to whatever you're making. Sesame seeds are also incredible in savory spice blends, like Organic Everything Bagel Seasoning. In Japan, sesame is an essential ingredient in the rice topping blend called Furikake.

A simple snack can be made with just three ingredients: your favorite dough, some honey, and some sesame seeds. This recipe is individual and made to whatever scale you want, so there are no exact measurements. Simply break your dough into small pieces, roll the pieces up and place on a baking tray or a baking pan. Bake at 350 until the balls begin to brown. While they are baking, make a mixture of honey and sesame seeds at whatever ratio you prefer. Add a lot of seeds if you love them, add only a few if you don't want your chewy dough balls to be as crunchy. Remove the balls from the oven and drizzle your honey and sesame seed mixture over them to taste. Enjoy the sweet, nutty flavor and the chewy texture of the dough balls! In a similar vein, Armernian Simit Cookies require a spattering of sesame seeds both for aesthetic and flavor.

If you enjoy making your own tahini, you can make it with these seeds. Tahini can then be used in homemade hummus recipes, whether they are sweet or savory. Tahini can also be used as a fruit and vegetable dip or as a spread on pita bread.

Sesame seeds need to be stored in a cool, dry place. They go rancid quickly if they are exposed to humidity or moisture in any way. Sesame oil on the other hand is very hearty and is ideal for cooking in warm to hot climates.

What Does Organic White Sesame Seed Taste Like?

Organic White Sesame Seeds are slightly nutty and have a nice, firm crunch when they are bitten into.

Substitutions and Conversions

You can use any sesame seed in place of white sesame seeds, with the only caveat being that Black Sesame Seeds are slightly more nutty than the lightly colored white seeds or toasted seeds.

output:
Pasilla de Oaxaca Chiles, Capsicum annuum, are hot chiles. They are also called pasilla de Oaxaca, pasilla de Oaxaca chile, pasilla mixe, or chile pasilla Oaxaqueño.
Pasilla de Oaxaca chiles are a major agricultural crop in that region Mexican state of Oaxaca. These chiles are farmed primarily on small-holdings properties, and are called ayuuk (pronounced “ah-YOOK”) by the locals. These locations and the processing areas where they are cleaned, dried, and smoked are fiercely protected by the locals to prevent the seeds and drying techniques from theft.
Pasilla de Oaxaca Chiles are popular with Mexican, American, and Japanese restaurants; cafes; breweries; catering companies; manufactures of bitters and cocktail mixes; and independent spice shops.
There are typically 3 Pasilla de Oaxaca Chiles per ounce.
One whole Pasilla de Oaxaca Chile = approximately two teaspoons of powder when ground.

Flavor Profile
Pasilla de Oaxaca Chiles deliver a deep, smoky flavor that can almost mimic the savory notes of pork. They deliver hints of tobacco and fruit, and a late heat that lingers.

How To Use
With their strangely meaty aroma, Pasilla de Oaxaca Chiles are useful for imparting umami, pork-like flavor into foods, including this Chile Marinated Pork Oaxaca Style. Use these chiles to season black beans for a rich-tasting Oaxacan Tlayuda without the meat, or in a smoky Pasilla De Oaxaca Black Bean Dip. They are also wonderful in Smoky Oaxacan Shrimp and Grits and Easy Borracho Beans.
Add Pasilla de Oaxaca Chiles to sauces like mole, soups, and salsas, or homemade taco seasonings. These chiles pair well with garlic, onions, allspice, epazote, cilantro, tomatillo, black beans, chicken, cocoa, coriander, and sesame seeds.

Pasilla Negro Chiles (pronounced "pah-SEE-yah"), Capsicum annuum, are also referred to as chile negro, chile pasilla, pasilla negro or pasilla pepper. Pasilla translates to "little raisin" due to its dark, wrinkled skin. Many dried chiles are called one thing when dried and another when fresh; this chile is known as the chilaca (“chi-LA-ka”) chile when in its fresh state.
Pasilla Negro chiles are long and slender chiles that taper to a point. Dried pasilla peppers are dark purple or black and have a rich flavor. They’re often described as tasting of chocolate, prunes, or raisins.
There are approximately two dried Pasilla Negro Chiles per ounce. 1 Pasilla Negro Chile is equal to 1 Tablespoon of Pasilla Negro Chile Powder.
Frequent buyers of Pasilla Negro Chiles are Mexican, Latin American and American restaurants and cafes; breweries; independent spice shops; and companies that manufacture gourmet jams and sauces

The flavor of the Pasilla pepper is rich and fruity, with chocolate and raisin notes and woodsy undertones.

Heat Level
Pasilla chiles have a heat range of 1,000 to 2,000 SHU and are considered mild heat chiles.

How to Use
Make Mexico’s signature dish, Mole Poblano, with the help of Pasilla Negro Chiles. Stir into tortilla soup or Pozole Rojo. Use them to give extra depth to Vegetarian Bean Chili or Red Enchilada Sauce. Pair this with black beans in a Black Bean and Chorizo Breakfast Burrito or make an impossibly rich Sour Cream Chicken Enchilada Casserole.
Pasilla Negro Chiles can be rehydrated and stuffed with flavorful blends of meats and cheeses. Once dehydrated, they can also be made into a paste or puree and added to adobos, chili, cream sauces, seafood chowder, salsas, enchilada sauce, or mole sauce. Pasilla peppers can also be toasted and ground into a Pasilla chile powder for further use.

Pizza originated in Naples, a simple flatbread topped with fresh cheese, perhaps some anchovies, seasonal vegetables, and the herbs and spices that make these simple ingredients sing. This blend combines classic Mediterranean flavors that embrace pizza’s Neapolitan history and makes it easy to enjoy one of the world’s most popular dishes.

How To Use
Pizza Seasoning is incredibly versatile and is helpful at any stage of cooking. If you are making pizza at home, mix some of this blend into your pizza dough for an out-of-this-world pizza crust. Stir it into a vegetarian version of Bolognese. Knead some into your meatloaf. This blend would make a great flavor base for a veggie-packed minestrone or Tortellini Soup. These Grade A1 Poppy Seeds are grown specifically for culinary purposes and should not be confused with the pharmaceutical-grade opium poppy. These seeds are procured from a seed pod and straw that contain an extremely low level of opiates. To protect the integrity of the hull and oil content of the seeds they are unwashed and untreated, but if seeds come in contact with poppy milk during harvest, the milk will not cause an opiate contamination.

Our Poppy Seeds are frequently purchased by bakeries, bagel shops, restaurants, cafes, food trucks, coffee shops and spice shops.

Flavor Profile

Subtle nutty flavor with a light sweetness that intensifies when roasted or toasted.

How To Use

We recommend dry-roast poppy seeds in a pan before using to make the flavor blossom. Poppy seeds are ubiquitous with bread toppings, so sprinkle them liberally over bagels, Soft Pretzels, or Dill Focaccia Bread. Throw them in your sourdough discard with some rosemary for rustic homemade crackers. Create texture and contrast by stirring them into Lemon Rice. They’re fun in Indian food, so use them to garnish Butter Chicken or Vegetable Curry. Grind into paste and bake into a sweet, yeasted dough for a classic Eastern European poppy seed roll.

Poppy seeds pair well with honey, butter, allspice, cardamom, coriander, fennel, and turmeric.

Create unforgettable Hash Browns with the addition of ½ teaspoon Porcini Mushroom Powder. Mix Porcini Mushroom Powder in with breadcrumbs and sprinkle on macaroni and cheese.
Porcini Mushroom Powder adds deep and hearty flavor to pizza, homemade pasta and pasta sauce, eggs, potatoes, DIY seasoning blends, barbecue rubs, grilled meats and seafood, rice dishes, soups, stews, and cheeses.

instruction: Write a product description in the Spices, Inc. brand voice for the following blend.
input:
Name: Pork Stank
Category: Seasoning Blends
Cuisine: American
Characteristics: Barbecue Rubs, BBQ Rubs and Grill Seasonings, Olive Oil Shop Top 50 Seasonings, Pork, White Label Products
Ingredients: sugar, sea salt, paprika, yellow mustard, onion, garlic, grains of paradise, black pepper, rosemary, ancho, marjoram, guajillo, cloves, allspice, cumin
output:
Pork Stank has been one of our top-selling pork rubs since we added it to our lineup over a decade ago. It was created for us by the owner of a competition barbecue team who also ran a successful barbecue catering business.
This is a flavorful all-purpose pork rub and is more sweet than hot, like many great pork rubs. This 16-ingredient pork rub has won competitions up and down the east coast in both the pork butt and pork rib categories. We tested this in our test kitchen using pork shoulder. We tasted it without sauce to get the pork rub’s full flavor. Our kitchen taste testers claimed it was perfect.

Flavor Profile
Pork Stank is sweet and earthy with some herby undertones and a very mild back-of-the-throat heat.

How to Use
When using Pork Stank as a pork rub, you can apply it in advance, with some people liking to apply it 8-24 hours before smoking. The truth is that most of the rub's molecules are too large and will penetrate less than a 1/2" into the meat during this time.
A good pork rub is meant more as a surface treatment for flavor and to create the bark. We like to apply the rub just before cooking with a thin layer of oil (olive, canola, or vegetable oil all work well), as most of the flavors in the rub are oil soluble. Spread the rub generously on the thicker portions of the shoulder.
You want to maximize the flavor when smoking large cuts of pork butts because these roasts have a great deal of meat compared to the available surface area. You need to get the most out of your rub and apply as much of the Pork Stank into the meat as it will hold.
One trick we did learn from our time working with the competition barbecuers was to add two tablespoons of Pork Stank to one cup of apple juice to spray on the meat while it is smoking.
Once the pork butt hits 150 to 160°F, the moisture from inside the meat starts to move to the surface and begins evaporating, which cools the surface of the meat. This is what starts drying the exterior and helps form the bark.
If you're not familiar with a pork shoulder, there are two halves, the "Boston butt" (also called the pork butt) and the "picnic ham.” The "butt" comes from the top half of the shoulder, from the back of the pig near the spine through the shoulder blade.
Butts normally weigh between 4 and 14 pounds and typically have shoulder blade bones, although some butchers will remove the bones and sell them as "boneless butts.” Calling it, a butt seems odd since it comes from the front of the hog. But make no mistake, when seasoned and smoked correctly, this portion of the hog provides the tastiest meat for pulled pork sandwiches.
In addition to pork butts and pork ribs, this Pork Stank is equally delicious on ham and pork chops.

Stir this into a stuffing or a savory bread pudding for a festive side dish, or add to stuffed mushrooms or creamed onions.
